newsitem.title: FRANCE: Clarins in convertible bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Clarins in convertible bond issue.

text.p: Skin care and cosmetics firm Clarins said it would issue between one million and 1,150,000 convertible bonds at a price of 890 francs each for a total amount of between 890 million and 1.023 billion francs.
It said in a statement the bonds were zero-coupon and had a life of 15 years.
The bonds will be reimbursed at a price of 1,336.96 for an actuatial rate of 2.75 percent.
The conversion will be at the rate of one share for one bond and converion is possible from February 21, 1997.
Existing shareholders have a priority to subscribe to the bonds between February 6 and 12.
Merril Lynch is the lead-manager of the so-called LYON (liquid yield option notes) issue.
HSBC Investments was financial adviser to Clarins, for whom the issue is the first bond loan.
